title: Introduce compact-shuttle compaction and soft-partitioning for KV cache
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: GPU KV caches are increasingly fragmented under continuous-batching workloads with mixed sequence lengths. Fragmentation leads to wasted device memory, suboptimal batching density, and intermittent allocation failures that force fallback to slower model variants. Existing approaches (aggressive full compaction, coarse-grain slabing) either cause latency spikes or leave long-lived holes that accumulate over time.

Proposal (compact-shuttle + soft-partitioning):
- Compact-shuttle: a low-priority background agent that incrementally migrates long-lived KV segments to contiguous GPU regions without requiring a global stop-the-world compaction. The shuttle moves small 'micro-chunks' (configurable, default 256KB) and performs in-place metadata remapping to maintain existing pointers. Migration is rate-limited by token throughput and piggybacks on idle GPU copies (cudaMemcpyAsync) to avoid interfering with hot inference paths.
- Soft-partitioning: classify KV allocations into fast/compactible vs sticky/cold partitions based on access-frequency windows and sequence-length histograms. Soft partitions are advisory (no strict barriers) so hot entries can flow between partitions when access patterns change. This reduces cross-fragmentation between short-lived and long-lived entries.
- Spill-to-host fallback: when GPU device fragmentation prevents satisfying a large prefix allocation, the runtime will transparently spill selected cold segments to host memory (pinned) and keep a lightweight handle on-device. This avoids immediate allocation failures and gives compact-shuttle time to reclaim contiguous device space. Spill candidates are chosen to minimize copy-back frequency (LRU with coldness hysteresis).

Why this is different: instead of coarse large-scale defragmentation windows or complex indirection layers, compact-shuttle focuses on micro-migrations during low-utilization quanta and combines that with a soft partitioning policy to segregate traffic types. The design aims to minimize peak latency impact and overall GPU-to-host traffic while noticeably lowering fragmentation entropy over days of continuous traffic.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Complexity: micro-migration requires careful pointer remapping and strong invariants to avoid cache-corruption.
- Copy costs: even rate-limited copies consume PCIe/NVLink bandwidth; on some configs (GPUDirect absent) spill traffic may hurt throughput.
- Latency spikes: mis-tuned migration bursts can cause micro-latency blips; mitigated via adaptive backoff and scheduling during low-percentile latency windows.
- Hardware variance: different GPUs (A100 vs H100) and interconnects change copy economics; policy must be hardware-aware.

Key metrics to track:
- Fragmentation ratio (device bytes free but unusable / total device bytes)
- Successful large-prefix allocation rate (per hour)
- Background copy bandwidth and copy/wait time distribution
- Latency p95/p99 before/during shuttle activity
- Spill frequency and average time-to-compact-back

Related docs and artifacts:
- Design doc (working): https://docs.google.com/document/d/compact-shuttle-design
- Perf dashboard (test cluster): https://grafana.redwood-internal/runtime/kv-frag-compact-shuttle
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2147
implementation_plan: 1) Small experiment phase (week 1): add micro-chunk migration API and in-memory metadata remapping layer behind an opt-in flag; unit tests for pointer safety.
2) Spike (week 2): implement simple soft-partition classifier based on last-N access samples and sequence-length histogram; run on canary serving nodes.
3) Integrate spill-to-host path (week 3): pinned-host buffer management and spill policy with telemetry; safety checks for copy-back.
4) Rate-limiter and scheduler (week 4): adaptive pacing using background utilization and tail-latency signals; per-GPU policy knobs.
5) End-to-end tests (week 5): stress tests with mixed sequences, continuous-batching harness, and fault injection (mid-migration backup/rollback).
6) Gradual rollout (weeks 6–8): feature-flagged rollout to Dedicated pools, monitor metrics, tune heuristics, add canary alerts and automated rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: A. Fragmentation ratio reduced by >=30% on 48-hour mixed workload compared to baseline without compact-shuttle.
B. Rate of large-prefix allocation failures reduced by >=90% in canary clusters.
C. No increase in p99 token latency >5% during steady-state under default pacing; documented knobs to trade latency for reclamation speed.
D. Spill-to-host path used only for cold segments and average spill-to-compact-back latency < 10 minutes under typical workload.
E. End-to-end tests and PRs merged with required safety checks and feature-flag gating.
